mike: heads up — after the kernel selector change (PR #4120) we've seen increased GPU memory fragmentation and a ~12% drop in prefix-cache hit-rate on p99 paths. attaching heap profile and kernel routing log.

sophia: yikes. can you paste the profiler output?

mike: short summary: kernel-routing started preferring `fast_attention_v2` for seq<=128. that kernel needs larger temporary workspace per request and allocs are more frequent. allocator snapshots show many small free slabs and a growing number of non-contiguous free blocks -> fragmentation. pprof snippets attached in thread.

lee: do we have hit/miss broken down by TTL buckets? curious if evictions are coming from aggressive TTL sweeps vs memory reclamation.

mike: yes — quick numbers: pre-deploy hit-rate 78% (global), post-deploy 66%. TTL distribution shows a spike of evictions at age 4–7s. current config is `prefix_cache.shard_count=128`, `ttl=10s`, `per_shard_cap=64MB`.

eva: a few low-risk mitigations to try: 1) drop shard_count to 64 so each shard keeps a larger contiguous working set, 2) enable buffer reuse on the workspace pool (`reuse=true`) to reduce churn, 3) add a light-weight compaction step on eviction to coalesce free ranges.

jun: + check batching heuristics — with the kernel change we may be producing smaller batches (kernel latency tradeoffs) which increases alloc frequency. options: reduce `min_batch_fill` to 2 or increase batching window to 10ms to amortize workspace cost.

mike: concrete symptom: OOMs start when workspace_pool can't recycle buffers fast enough. sample allocator log: 
```
[2026-03-17T21:42:03Z] Allocator: total_free=1.3MB, largest_free=32KB, requested=1.2MB -> fail, triggering OOM path
[2026-03-17T21:42:03Z] PromptCache: evicted 48 items from shard=73, freed=1.1MB
```
we're seeing many small frees not usable for the larger workspace requests.

cache-bot: perf-regression alert: prefix-cache hit-rate down 12% in `us-east-1` since deploy at 2026-03-14T01:22Z. OOM count up x3 on p99 machines.

sophia: proposed test plan: A/B on a canary pool. control: `shards=128, ttl=10s, reuse=false`; candidate: `shards=64, ttl=15s, reuse=true, compact_on_eviction=true`. Metrics: p99 latency, cache_hit, oom_count, allocation churn. run for 2h steady traffic using the replay harness. I can spin up the canary.

mike: i'll prepare profiling hooks and the kernel-selection override so we can toggle kernel back to `fast_attention_v1` if needed. will also capture `cudaMalloc`/free traces. anyone own the canary run? :eyes:

lee: i'll own it tonight and kick off the two pools. will add the metrics dashboard (per-shard hit heatmap + allocator fragmentation metric). :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: canary job scheduled: job-id=cb-1765437890, start=2026-03-17T22:00:00Z

mike: thanks — once we have data we'll iterate. i'll also add short-term mitigation to the runtime: prefer `fast_attention_v1` for seq<=64 until we verify buffer reuse gains. adding notes to runbook `/docs/runbooks/prefix-cache-budgeting.md` :spiral_notepad:
